intro: There is no motor, no sensor and no app, so there is very little to break. Every problem with this box is a litter problem or a technique problem.

symptoms.title: Clumps do not fall into the tray
symptoms.summary: You roll the box but clumps stay in the litter bed instead of dropping through the grate.
causes: Litter is not clumping hard enough — cheap clay breaks up on the roll.
The bed is too shallow, so urine reaches the plastic and smears.
The box was not rolled fully onto its side.

fixes.detail: This design depends entirely on clumps holding together. Budget litter is a false economy here.
Three inches minimum. Shallow beds are the usual cause.
Roll until the box is fully on its side and hold for two seconds before rolling back.

symptoms.escalate: There is no mechanism to fail here — if clumps still will not drop, the litter is the variable to change.

symptoms.title: Litter and waste stuck in the seams
symptoms.summary: Material collects where the two halves join and does not clear on rolling.
causes: This is inherent to the two-piece design.
The halves are not clipped fully together, widening the seam.
Litter is too fine and packs into the joint.

fixes.detail: Unclip the halves and wash both with warm water and unscented soap.
Press all clips home. A partly open seam collects far more material.
Fine-grain litter packs into the joint; a coarser clay does not.

symptoms.escalate: Not a fault. It is the maintenance cost of a $45 box with no motor.
